scores.evidence: Strong base, verified against the repo: docs/README.md gives every document a status (current/frozen/historical/superseded), a reading order for each of four audiences, and a 'Known discrepancies in historical records' section (agency size 40 vs 50, harness commit history, $4.29 vs $3.55, EUR 5-6k vs EUR 3 990-4 200, creative scope, untracked DECK.md). docs/OPERATING_DECISIONS.md is named as the authority that overrides older text and is used consistently: README 'Where the project stands', GO_LIVE_DECISIONS R-1..R-6, TIERS Tier 8. The published test figures are correct: I ran the suite and got '948 passed, 7 skipped, 48 xfailed', matching CLAUDE.md:18, README.md:194, TIERS.md:140 and tier_8_report.md:83. Every relative link in the front doors and in docs/ (README, START_HERE, WALKTHROUGH, docs/*.md, docs/pilot/*.md) points at a tracked file; the only broken links are in tools/walkthrough history notes. Routing-era labelling is systematic: the COST_MODEL.md era banner, the EVIDENCE.md 'Routing era' box, EVAL_RECORD.md [committed]/[local store] tags. The Tiers 5-8 commands are documented in README 'Agency operations' and linked to the docs/pilot guides. AGENTS.md is now a correct pointer, and HANDOFF_WALKTHROUGH.md sits in docs/history with a superseded banner. The weakness is that the round-1 truth sweep is incomplete. tier_8_report.md:71 says routing-validate-01's 'citations relabelled committed', yet contradictory statements survive in current-status documents.
defects: docs/EVIDENCE.md contradicts itself on the same run. Lines 3-5 list 'the one current-routing extraction leg' among figures from 'local runs which are not in the repository'. Lines 82-85 say runs/routing-validate-01 'is committed evidence (32 KB, synthetic)'. `git ls-files` confirms it is committed.
WALKTHROUGH.html:1293 (sheet 10 body) says the 598 743-token leg is 'one local run not committed'. The ledger on the same sheet (the decision-2 text) and docs/README.md:81 say it is committed.

WALKTHROUGH.html:733 (sheet 03 footnote) states in the present tense that 'runtime agents retain Read access to its containing directory' (the answer-key folder). Since Tier 8 this is false: pipeline/agents.py:228 adds a Read/Write/Edit deny rule for any answer_key.json, and runner.stage_inputs stages copies that exclude the key. Sheet 08 and docs/SECURITY.md say so.

runs/tier_8_report.md header still reads 'Branch: round1-integration ... not committed by the integrator; the orchestrator commits', but it is commit 1aaa560 on main. docs/README.md's 'Known discrepancies' list does not note this.

Step-count inconsistency across the front doors: WALKTHROUGH sheet 02 says 'Nine steps, three roles', while START_HERE.html and SHARE_ME.html (generated by pipeline/share.py) say 'Ten steps, two of them people'.

tools/walkthrough/ top level still holds ~40 codex_*.md/.log/_prompt.md files, image variants and a near-duplicate of the paper (a_brief_with_receipts.html). Many of these carry absolute /Users/chrism/... links or repo-relative links that break from that folder. docs/README.md only says 'the rest is review-loop history', and none of them has been moved to archive/ as the scorer scripts were.
scores.to_reach_9: Fix the three stale statements (EVIDENCE.md intro, WALKTHROUGH sheet 10 body, WALKTHROUGH sheet 03 footnote), add the tier_8 header note to docs/README.md 'Known discrepancies', and align the step count. Add an automated consistency test so the next sweep cannot miss such statements: one facts file, plus assertions that every run cited as committed is git-tracked and no front door says otherwise. Archive the tools/walkthrough history files behind a README.

scores.evidence: WALKTHROUGH.html is a real decision paper. It puts the answer first: sheet 01 leads with 'Approve a four-week pilot, with live use in week 4 conditional on the retrospective results', and sheet 10 asks for three decisions, each with an owner and a deadline ('owner: the executive sponsor named at kickoff · needed before week 1'). It separates measured from assumed: the EUR 4.0-4.2k/yr figure is derived explicitly from PRD A1/A2/A4, and PRD §10's EUR 5-6k is shown to be inconsistent. It names what stays human: the red pen, sign-off and a separate creative approver, and it shows the three conflicts resolved with the resolver's initials. It states limits and risks: 'Exam-green is not lead-ready', 15/17 then 16/17 on voreas, refusals 3 of 10, Draft A's invented budget, 'Not proven: generative quality under the current routing, Greek register, review time, adoption'. The walkthrough gate passes (tools/walkthrough/checks.py: 10 sheets, 0 failures). START_HERE.html and SHARE_ME.html give a hiring panel a clear what / proved / not proved / decision section and disclose the KNOWN_DEFECTS B3 flag drop. Tier reports 5-8 record DoD, deferred items and resolved model IDs (gpt-6-astra for development review, claude-opus-5-5 at Tier 8, runtime IDs), and the Tier 8 report ends with explicit boundaries. A board-materials specialist would still flag the headline numbers, one internal contradiction, and an economics gap.
defects: The headline usage figure is not labelled with its routing era where it carries the most weight. The sheet 01 tile (WALKTHROUGH.html:533) presents 0.98 M tokens/brief and '15 million' a month as 'the figure to hold against a plan's usage window', and the sheet 10 '~15M tokens a month' tile repeats the phrase. The same paper shows that the one current-routing leg measured roughly double (598 743 vs 295 774). Scaling every extraction leg by that ratio gives about 1.5 M tokens per brief, so a sponsor who remembers only the tile will under-plan capacity by about half. The caveat exists only in decision 3's text and in sheet 02.

The paper contradicts itself on sheet 10: the body calls routing-validate-01 'one local run not committed', while the ledger calls it committed. Sheet 03 still says agents can read the answer-key folder, while sheet 08 says they cannot. In a paper whose selling point is 'receipts', a reader who spots either will discount the rest.

The paper asks for approval without an economic frame. Benefit is about EUR 4.0-4.2k/yr (an assumption), and costs are 'not yet estimated', with a spending ceiling deferred to a pre-week-1 condition. There is no indicative cost envelope for the pilot: lead hours for 6 retro projects, champion training, operator time, seats. There is no break-even line and no statement of the non-labour value (errors caught: 3 conflicts, 4 gaps, an invented total struck) that would justify a pilot whose labour value is small.

The main text is dense for a non-engineer. The sheet bodies (not only the ledgers) use check IDs (T2.4, T2.6, X3), 'verify-extract', 'resumed legs', 'model-agent attempts, each potentially containing multiple turns' and cache percentages, and there is no glossary. Sheet 01 does explain tokens well, but that is the exception.

SHARE_ME.html, the page for 'anyone without the repo', describes the three decisions in prose but does not carry the decision paper. A forwarded sponsor cannot see the owners, deadlines or pilot targets without cloning the repo.
WALKTHROUGH (nine steps) and START_HERE/SHARE_ME (ten steps) describe the flow differently.
scores.to_reach_9: On sheets 01 and 10, label every headline number with its era ('graded July routing; current routing unmeasured, one leg ~2x'), and add a clearly marked estimated range for current-routing usage, or replace the tiles once the re-baseline lands. Fix the two internal contradictions. Add a one-box economics panel to sheet 10: indicative pilot cost envelope, break-even condition, stop criteria, and the non-labour value. Move check IDs and engineering terms into the ledgers or a glossary. Let SHARE_ME carry a compact decision page.

moves.title: Finish the round-1 truth sweep: three stale statements and one header note
moves.rationale: These are the only concrete contradictions between current documents and the code or git state that I could find. Each one is cheap to fix, and each undermines the 'receipts' credibility the paper is built on.

WALKTHROUGH.html:1293: replace 'one local run not committed' with 'one committed run (runs/routing-validate-01)'. WALKTHROUGH.html:733: change 'runtime agents retain Read access to its containing directory' to 'in the July run agents could still read its folder; since round 1 they read staged copies that exclude it, under a deny rule (docs/SECURITY.md §3.2)'. docs/README.md 'Known discrepancies': add that runs/tier_8_report.md's header ('Branch: round1-integration ... not committed') predates its commit 1aaa560 on main. moves.title: Label the headline usage and time tiles with their routing era, with a marked estimated range
moves.rationale: The sheet 01 and sheet 10 tiles present a July-routing figure as 'the figure to hold against a plan's usage window', although the paper's own evidence shows the current routing at about 2x on the one measured leg. A board paper's headline must not understate a known quantity.

Add one line clearly marked ESTIMATE, NOT MEASURED: 'if every source behaves like the one re-measured leg (x2.02), about 1.5 M per brief, about 22 M a month'. moves.title: Add an economics and stop-criteria box to sheet 10
moves.rationale: The ask is 'approve a pilot' for an assumed EUR 4.0-4.2k/yr of labour value, with costs unestimated. A decision maker needs the cost envelope of the pilot itself, a break-even condition and the non-labour value, or the rational answer is 'come back with numbers'.
moves.concrete_changes: WALKTHROUGH.html sheet 10: add a panel listing (a) the pilot's indicative internal effort from docs/pilot/ROLES.md and SCORECARD.md (2 leads x 3 retro projects x review time, champion training per T-06, operator hours per run), labelled estimate; (b) the break-even statement 'annual running cost (seats plus support) must stay below the validated labour value, EUR ~4k at PRD assumptions, or the case rests on quality alone'; (c) the non-labour value evidenced in this run: 3 conflicts surfaced, 4 gaps turned into questions, an invented creative total caught; (d) the explicit stop criteria already in SCORECARD/GO_LIVE_DECISIONS (D-14, D-18) in one line. Mirror the lines in docs/pilot/GO_LIVE_DECISIONS.md. No new claims: every figure is either cited or marked estimate.

moves.rationale: Round 1's sweep claimed completeness and still missed three statements. A deterministic check makes document currency a gate instead of a manual chore.
moves.concrete_changes: New docs/facts.json holding the canonical figures (test counts, 17/17, 15/17 then 16/17, 12/12, 984 820, 1 134 734, 598 743, 295 774, EUR 3 990-4 200) and each cited run's committed/local status. New tests/test_doc_consistency.py that (1) asserts every run directory marked committed is in `git ls-files` and every one marked local is not; (2) fails when README.md, START_HERE.html, SHARE_ME.html, WALKTHROUGH.html, CLAUDE.md, docs/*.md or docs/pilot/*.md mention a committed run next to 'not committed' or 'local'; (3) fails when a figure pattern appears in those files with a value that differs from facts.json (ignoring docs/history, runs/tier_*_report.md and other historical records). overall: The documentation set is unusually disciplined for an MVP. It has a status-labelled index with per-audience reading orders, an authoritative decision log, routing-era labels on every figure, a known-discrepancies register, and published test counts that reproduce exactly (948/7/48). The walkthrough is a genuine answer-first decision paper that separates measured from assumed and keeps people visibly in charge. Both aspects stop at 7 for concrete, fixable reasons. First, the round-1 sweep left contradictions in current documents: EVIDENCE.md calls routing-validate-01 both local and committed, WALKTHROUGH sheet 10 calls it 'not committed', and sheet 03 says agents can read the answer-key folder. Second, the sponsor-facing headline tiles present the July-routing 0.98 M tokens and 15 M/month as the planning figure without an era label, although the paper's own evidence points to about 1.5 M per brief under the current routing. Third, the pilot ask has no cost envelope, break-even or stop line against a small (about EUR 4k/yr) assumed labour value. The first two moves are small and would remove most of the gap.
